parts.visual:
A startup spends $5 Million and officially dies. The founder does not hide in shame. Instead, they write a massive, public 10-page essay detailing exactly why the company failed, the mistakes they made, and what they learned. They email it to all their investors.

The Autopsy:
1. The Post-Mortem: A formal, objective analysis of a failed project or a dead company to determine the root causes of the failure.
2. The Silicon Valley Culture: In elite tech circles, failure is not a sin; but failing to *learn* from the failure is unforgivable.
parts.audio: A post-mortem transforms a $5 Million total loss into a $5 Million education. By writing down exactly why you failed, you process the grief, protect your reputation, and prove to investors that you are smarter now than you were three years ago.

questions.question: What is the most common root cause of startup failure cited in Post-Mortems?
options: Building a product no one actually wanted (No Product-Market Fit). Running out of cash is just the symptom; the disease was spending three years building software in a vacuum without ever talking to paying customers.
questions.correct_answer: Building a product no one actually wanted (No Product-Market Fit). Running out of cash is just the symptom; the disease was spending three years building software in a vacuum without ever talking to paying customers.
questions.explanation: The market is a harsh teacher.

questions.question: Listen to the founder's Post-Mortem. What critical mistake did they make regarding their team?
questions.tts_text: We failed because my co-founder and I were too similar. We were both visionary designers. We built a beautiful app, but neither of us knew how to write the backend database code or how to sell it to businesses. We were a broken puzzle.
options: Lack of complementary skills. Two visionary designers cannot build a scalable software company alone. A great post-mortem identifies not just market failures, but deep organizational blind spots.
questions.correct_answer: Lack of complementary skills. Two visionary designers cannot build a scalable software company alone. A great post-mortem identifies not just market failures, but deep organizational blind spots.
questions.explanation: A team of five strikers cannot win a soccer match.

questions.question: Why is it strategic for a founder to publish their Post-Mortem publicly (e.g., on Medium or X)?
options: It controls the narrative and signals maturity. If you don't tell the story, rumors will. A brutally honest, public post-mortem shows extreme self-awareness. VCs respect founders who can publicly dissect their own failures.
To get a refund from the VCs.

options: 'We hired the wrong VP of Sales.'
